66.title: [P1] Do not execute mutable issue content as trusted AFK instructions
66.body:
<!-- ralph-milestone-finding pr:61 id:422a13f32d983df171ec -->
## Context

**Source:** automated milestone review of PR #61
**Milestone:** Phase 1: Core Profile API (Tracer Bullet)
**Reviewed head:** `aa63f8a3c103ac93e75c485e2b84e4918cf944ac`
**Severity:** P1
**Location:** `scripts/ralph/ralph-loop.mjs:975`

## Finding

Issue bodies are copied verbatim into a workspace-write Codex prompt without validating author association or an approved content hash. An external issue author can edit the body after milestone assignment; generated changes are subsequently validated outside the sandbox, committed, and pushed by a credentialed process. Restrict inputs to trusted authors or immutable approved snapshots, sanitize the child environment, and execute generated validation scripts in a credential-free isolation boundary.

## Definition of done

- Fix the root cause without weakening existing behavior or tests.
- Add or update regression coverage for the failure path.
- Run the relevant checks from AGENTS.md and the Ralph configuration.
- Keep the change focused on this finding; do not create a pull request.

The existing draft PR will be updated and reviewed again after all review findings are resolved.

<!-- ralph-issue-review-context:start -->
## Ralph Loop: independent review found problems

HEAD is the claimed commit, but the trust and validation boundaries remain incomplete. The targeted author test passes; the full Ralph suite is blocked here by read-only sandbox temp-directory restrictions.

- **P1 — Creator allowlist still trusts later mutable edits** (scripts/ralph/ralph-loop.mjs:1013)
  `issue.user.login` identifies the original opener, while the title/body are fetched live. Users with issue-management permission can edit an existing issue without changing that opener ([GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues)). Thus an untrusted triage user can alter an issue created by a trusted account and have its new content pass this check into the workspace-write prompt. Pin and verify an approved title/body hash or immutable snapshot at assignment (or verify a trusted editor for each revision).
- **P1 — Validation runs on the credentialed host, not in a credential-free isolation boundary** (scripts/ralph/ralph-loop.mjs:1899)
  Removing selected environment variables before `npm run` is not an isolation boundary: each generated validation script still executes as the host user, with host filesystem access, network access, and any OS-backed/Git credential helpers available to that user. A changed package script can therefore use credentials that are not environment variables. Run validations in an actual isolated container/VM or dedicated uncredentialed OS account with a constrained workspace mount and network policy.
- **P2 — The regression test does not exercise the AFK execution path** (scripts/ralph/ralph-loop.test.mjs:33)
  The new test calls the exported `assertTrustedIssue` helper directly. It does not prove that `runCodex` rejects an untrusted freshly fetched or recovery issue before spawning Codex, so removing the call at line 1708 or dropping author metadata during fetching would leave the test green. Add an end-to-end orchestration test with a fake Codex executable and assert it is never started for an untrusted issue.
<!-- ralph-issue-review-context:end -->
